name: @kitr/desktop
description: @kitr/desktop: the desktop platform with an Electron shell. Main and preload in platforms/<name>/, typed IPC, storage drivers, packaging with electron-builder.

kitr.name: desktop
kitr.title: Desktop
kitr.summary: Ship the same app to Windows, macOS and Linux in an Electron shell: Chromium ships with the app, so it renders the same everywhere.

platform.label: Electron
platform.tagline: Windows, macOS and Linux in an Electron shell. Chromium ships with the app, so it looks and behaves the same on every machine.

highlights.title: Your app, in a window
highlights.text: The same `app/` folder runs in the shell. The main and preload processes live in `platforms/app/`, and electron-builder packages the installers.

highlights.title: Typed IPC
highlights.text: One schema in `platforms/app/ipc.ts`: `handleIpc()` implements it in main and `createIpcClient()` calls it from your components, typed both ways.

highlights.title: Storage that lives on disk
highlights.text: Storage items write to `kitr-storage.json` in the app data folder instead of `localStorage`. Your code does not change.

highlights.title: The recommended desktop shell
highlights.text: What you test is what every user runs. Pick Tauri instead when download size matters more than identical rendering.
